summary: To let people take water from a well in the street on Shabbos, we may put corner boards around it. Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Meir argue how many boards are needed and how big the gaps may be.

chunks.en: We may put boards around wells: four corner pieces,
chunks.explain: Each corner piece is two boards joined in an L shape.
chunks.st: One may arrange upright boards [passin] around a well
chunks.stMore: in the public domain in order to permit drawing water from the well on Shabbat. A well is usually at least four handbreadths wide and ten handbreadths deep. Therefore, it is considered a private domain, and it is prohibited to draw water from it on Shabbat, as that would constitute a violation of the prohibition to carry from a private domain into a public one. The Sages therefore instituted that a virtual partition may be built in the area surrounding the well, so that the enclosed area could be considered a private domain, thus permitting use of the well and carrying of the water within the partitioned area. In this specific instance, the Sages demonstrated special leniency and did not require a proper partition to enclose the entire area.

chunks.en: that look like eight boards,

summary: The boards may be close to the well, as long as a cow can fit its head and most of its body inside. They may also be far away, if more boards are added.

chunks.en: We may put the boards close to the well,
chunks.st: It is permitted to bring the posts closer to the well,

chunks.en: as long as a cow can have its head
chunks.st: provided that the enclosed area is large enough for a cow to stand with its head

chunks.en: and most of its body inside while it drinks.
chunks.st: and the majority of its body inside the partitioned space while it drinks.

chunks.en: We may move them as far away as we want,
chunks.st: It is permitted to distance the boards from the well and expand the enclosed area by any amount,
chunks.stMore: i.e., as much as one wishes,

chunks.en: as long as we add more boards.
chunks.st: provided that he increases the number of upright boards between the double posts.

summary: Rabbi Yehudah says the boards around a well may hold in only a small field. The Sages say that limit is only for a garden or storage yard, but not for a place where people or animals stay.

chunks.st: The partitioned area may be expanded up to an area of two beit se’a,
chunks.stMore: which is an area of five thousand square cubits.

words.note: A beis sasayim is a field where two se'ah of seed are planted, 50 by 100 amos.

chunks.en: and for the others we make a belt ten tefachim tall.
chunks.explain: A belt is a fence of ropes all around.
chunks.st: But for the others, that is, a public cistern or a private well, one must set up a belt, i.e., a partition consisting of ropes, ten handbreadths high.
chunks.stMore: Such an arrangement creates a proper partition based on the principle of lavud, namely, that solid surfaces with gaps between them smaller than three handbreadths are considered joined.

summary: Rabbi Ila'i tells three things he heard from Rabbi Eliezer: about a very big garden, about someone who forgot to join the eiruv, and about a kind of maror for Pesach. No other student had heard them.
